rationale: C19 plausibly supplied a material administrative template: it defines classes of federal employees who may acquire competitive civil-service status based on prior appointment and service circumstances, incorporates agency-head involvement, and delegates implementing rules to the Civil Service Commission. The child generalizes essentially that machinery to a different class of incumbent employees and adds detailed service, performance, and examination conditions. C11 is closely related but is a one-person dispensation with much less reusable operative structure; C15 concerns Civil Service Commission administration of personnel rights but addresses expiration of reemployment rights rather than acquisition of competitive status.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The incumbent ... who is without competitive status shall, upon recommendation ... by the head of the agency in which he is employed, acquire a competitive civil service status if all of the following conditions are satisfied
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Any officer or employee ... who was ... serving under a war service indefinite or temporary indefinite appointment and who ... could, with the approval of the head of the agency in which he was serving, have been given a competitive status ... shall be considered as having a competitive status
shared_material.explanation: Both create conditional routes by which employees lacking ordinary competitive appointments obtain competitive status, with prior federal service and agency-head involvement central to eligibility.

shared_material.child_excerpt: such person successfully qualifies in such suitable noncompetitive examination as the Civil Service Commission may prescribe
shared_material.parent_excerpt: who is reached in regular order for probational appointment from a Civil Service register ... or who could ... have been given a competitive status under Civil Service Rule III
shared_material.explanation: Both use Civil Service qualification procedures to convert noncompetitive or temporary service into competitive status.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The Civil Service Commission shall promulgate regulations to effectuate the purposes of this order.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Civil Service Commission is authorized ... to prescribe such rules and regulations as may be necessary to carry out the provisions of this order
shared_material.explanation: The same implementing authority is assigned to the Civil Service Commission, completing the parallel administrative mechanism.
